newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank buys marks to press lev to peg fix.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank buys marks to press lev to peg fix.

text.p: The lev closed at 994-995 per mark, down from the opening's 989-994, as the central bank was seen buying marks to bring the exchange rate closer to the upcoming 1,000 levs-per-mark currency board peg, dealers said.

* The central bank was bidding for relatively large mark volumes at market rates on the local market also with the aim of boosting reserves of anchor currency ahead of the peg, to take effect from July 1.
* Central bank officials were unavailable to comment.
* The lev closed at 1,710-1,716 to the dollar, weaker than the morning's 1,705-1,712 as market makers adjusted the lev/dollar rate to the lev/mark and the international mark/dollar cross.

* From July 1 the lev will be pegged at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 to the mark as anchor in an IMF-prescribed currency board system designed to curb inflation, restore confidence in banks and stabilise the economy.

* Under the system levs in circulation must be precisely matched by central bank foreign exchange reserves and the central bank is committed to exchanging any amounts of its domestic monetary liabilities for marks.
* The mark share in the local forex market turnover has steadily risen in the past month while the dollar share has shrunk. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
